27 October 2026. Independent attack on the N952 interface.

STATUS AND SCIENTIFIC DECISION

This file establishes an exact full-law confidence geometry for a stationary
rank-two CP subfamily, and a matching-order native-call information lower bound.
It does not solve acquisition of arbitrary rank-r quantum instruments. It
separates avoidable coordinate-norm losses from genuine information cost, and
identifies an exactly optimal discriminating experiment. No historical novelty
or practical superiority is claimed.

S7 already establishes valid signed-coordinate perturbation and composition
bounds; S9 correctly preserves them. The S8 bounds are vacuous, but the raw
recorded counts are absent from this packet. This file does not pronounce the
rank-four fixture impossible or claim an improved certificate for it. S10
changes the physical interface and does not resolve this one.

1. LEGAL STATIONARY CP FAMILY

The hidden memory is a qubit with computational states 0 and 1. The supplied
family has an unknown scalar p in [0,1]. Each full-process start is state 0.
There are two legal actions:

 C (charge): 0 changes to 1 with probability p; 1 stays 1. Visible outcome 0.
 R (read): report the hidden bit nondestructively.

C has one visible branch with Kraus operators
 sqrt(1-p)|0><0|, sqrt(p)|1><0|, |1><1|.
The two R branches have Kraus operators |0><0| and |1><1|. The outcome sums
are TP; all maps are CP. Every coherence is discarded. This classical subfamily
of the quantum contract suffices for a lower bound on any full-class learner.

For p>0, reachable states span the diagonal two-dimensional space. Preparations
empty and C, and future tests empty and R=1, give
                  H_p = [[1,1],[0,p]].                            (1)
Predictive rank is exactly two. The inverse infinity norm is 1+1/p. Bad
short-core conditioning thus occurs at fixed rank with positive stationary
instruments. The family structure is a SUPPLIED restriction for our upper
bound. It is not learned from finitely many observed zeros. Only the lower
bound uses it merely as a contained subfamily of the full target class.

# Independent scientific review of frozen Q52 and Q17

27 October 2026. This review concerns the supplied frozen returns and the original scientific interface. It contains no policy or model ranking.

**Decision.** Q52 supports its general one-step analytic coercive inverse and its smoothed quadratic full-law theorem under the stated Gaussian divergence and regularity hypotheses. Its frozen cosine sampler has a valid exact-real, full-law fixture certificate after paid fitting and analytic verification. Q17 supports the pointwise inverse obstruction, including actual admissible first-order forcings without an L2 inverse, and its capped near-affine positive filling under an additional source promise. Both predictive-family theorems are supported at their stated family and reuse scopes. Neither return completes the general N687 value-query compiler or generic unknown-CP predictive acquisition. No further physical realization or external confirmation is required to accept these mathematical statements at these scopes. Historical novelty and practical advantage were not established by this review.

**Exposure and procedure.** The task itself identified these as native-Pro first returns and supplied the Q52/Q17 labels. Therefore this was not blind to that shared identity. I received no policy mapping or correspondence between the two labels and an orchestration action. Scientific source text mentions historical “Ultra” and “Luna” work, and packet prose mentions a colleague/helper; those are actual incidental exposures. I did not inspect memory, programme chats, dispatchers, Dots, policies/protocols, action/forecast/admission folders, warm continuations, live producers, or other review outputs. No messages, chats, goals, automations, or subagents were created.
